rule: module = the file's path below the scan root without extension and trailing `/index` (`src/chat` for src/chat/index.ts; basenames collide across directories): `src/app.f`, `src/app.C#m`, `#<init>`/`#<clinit>`/`#field` as in Java. | Imports, `require`, re-exports (`export *`, `export * as`) and workspace packages (package.json `exports`) resolve to the defining module; packages outside the scan are named as written (`node:http.createServer`, `zod.z.object`, medium). | Import statements are not calls. | **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding.
notes: a/index.js drops the trailing `/index`: module `a`, so `hello` is `a.hello`. a/util.js and b/util.js share a basename but are distinct modules `a/util` and `b/util` ('basenames collide across directories'). The aliased import `fmt as fmtB` resolves to `b/util.fmt`; the namespace import `autil.fmt(...)` resolves to `a/util.fmt` (imports resolve to the defining module), direct because the callee is a module function, not a method. `a/util.fmt` is reached from a/index.js and main.js with one ID (C1).
